title: Blends with offset WISE centroids make at least 72 percent of 951 field dwarfs with an extreme 12 um excess; unblended excess stars are often kinematically young and contain all three ZTF dust dimmers
abstract: Prior campaign work linked deep dust dimming of field dwarfs to extreme warm dust. It used 951 Gaia DR3 dwarfs at |b| > 20 deg with an AllWISE 12 um excess confirmed by Legacy Surveys (5.0e-5 of field dwarfs). ZTF showed 3 dust dimmers among them and 0 of 1,174 controls. We asked if this excess is dust around mature stars, dust around young stars, or blends. We compared Gaia tangential velocities with 10 matched controls per star (field model by extreme deconvolution plus a young component with 0.3 Gyr dispersions), and we measured the AllWISE-Gaia centroid offset against 3,000 controls at the same W1. The excess stars have young fraction 0.075 (0.038-0.110; held-out controls 0.04, up to 0.10). It is 0.55 (0.37-0.80) for 43 stars with bright photospheres (including TW Hya) and 0.00-0.04 for the 777 faintest. For faint photospheres the median offset is 0.22-0.38 arcsec against 0.06-0.08 arcsec for controls. At most 197 stars (269 at 95 percent) can be unblended, so at least 79 percent (72 percent) are blends. Offset stars have young fraction 0.00 (up to 0.05); clean stars 0.27 (0.18-0.40). Genuine extreme dust around field-kinematics dwarfs is at most 8.4e-6 (1.2e-5) of field dwarfs. All three dimmers are unblended: 3 of 150 unblended or bright stars dim (2.0 percent, 0.4-5.7; p = 0.0014), close to the covering chance of a ring with L_dust/L_star of 3-6 percent, and 0 of 484 offset stars. Two dimmers have young-like velocities; G4466 is old. Thus mature extreme dust is rare, and the dimming link holds for genuine dust. Limitations: the blend test gives bounds, not a per-star list; fixed young dispersions; no spectra; three dimmers. citations.reason: We reuse its candidate list, Legacy Surveys flags, ZTF vetting and field count. We show that at least 72 percent of its 951 excess stars are blends, which lowers its warm-dust rate for mature dwarfs, and that its dimmer-dust link becomes stronger for unblended stars.
